item.title: EDITORIAL: Investigation into Sylvia Luke needs full transparency
item.description: A public uproar has ensued over Lt. Gov. Sylvia Luke’s disclosure that in January 2022, while chair of the powerful House Finance Committee, she accepted $10,000 from a “constituent” at a dinner attended by Ty Cullen, then vice chair — and now a disgraced ex-con, having served federal prison time after admitting he accepted bribes repeatedly throughout his terms in the state Legislature.

item.title: Questions over Lt. Gov. Sylvia Luke likely to inspire challengers
item.description: Democratic and nonpartisan elected officials across the state are quietly calculating the financial and political costs of challenging Lt. Gov. Sylvia Luke by the June 2 filing deadline while suspicions swirl whether Luke is the target of an ongoing investigation by Hawaii’s attorney general.

item.title: Ready before the call: KPD upgrades officer training
item.description: LIHUE — Police officers on Kauai are using a state-of-the-art training facility to make safer, smarter decisions in the field.

item.title: HOOSER: The $35,000 in a paper bag story, and how it could impact Kauai
item.description: From a purely political perspective, Lt. Gov. Sylvia Luke is in a pretty tough spot.

item.title: Girl Scouts celebrate 100th anniversary of World Thinking Day
item.description: Monday, Presidents Day, was the 100th anniversary of World Thinking Day for the Girl Scouts, and one of the highlights of the activity at the Kukui Grove Center was a visit by a Girl Scout from the Philippines.

item.title: High school students push for safe spaces, opportunities
item.description: More than 80 public high school students filled the state Capitol Friday morning, not for a tour, but to press lawmakers with firsthand accounts of safety concerns and other issues they said could help boost success in and out of the classroom.
